fixes.explanation: Close, but it's False. The elders declare, "Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it." They say their eyes did not see it, so they're not claiming to be witnesses. If they had said they saw it, we'd have a whole different case on our hands. Moses tells them to say this while they wash their hands over the heifer (Deuteronomy 21:6–7).

That's right, baker. The elders declare, "Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it." They say it out loud, standing at the stream with their hands washed over the heifer. So no, they don't claim to have seen who killed the man. Say it with me: their eyes did not see it.

Actually it's True, friend. Moses says that when they do this, "…you have done what is right in the eyes of the LORD." The text gives them the thumbs up. I'd say that's a good word for Israel to hear after all those steps with the heifer and the stream.

I get the thinking, friend, but the text doesn't say anything about her people coming for her. Moses says the man must not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, and he gives one reason: "…since you have dishonored her." That's the reason the text states, and I won't add to it.

Right, baker. Moses says the father must acknowledge the firstborn "…by giving him a double portion of all that he has." That's a double portion of everything the father owns. And this is the son of the wife called unloved, so the text is clear that the father can't hand the right of the firstborn to the other wife's son instead (Deuteronomy 21:15–16).

Nope, friend, the text never mentions the mother asking the elders for anything. Moses says, "For that son is the firstfruits of his father’s strength; the right of the firstborn belongs to him." The right comes from him being the firstfruits of his father's strength. That's the reason Moses gives.

Right, baker. Moses says, "…you must not leave the body on the tree overnight, but you must be sure to bury him that day…" No overnight stay is allowed. The burial happens that very day. Moses also says the land is something the LORD is giving them as an inheritance, and they must not defile it (Deuteronomy 21:23).

Good thought, but the text gives a different deadline. Moses says, "…you must not leave the body on the tree overnight, but you must be sure to bury him that day…" He doesn't mention waiting for the elders at all. The text sets the time: that same day.
